label: GO step after a rewarded trial, when choosing a1, late in the episode (trials ~55-94)
explanation: Fires only at GO steps (never at D1/D2). It needs the previous trial to have been rewarded (prev_reward==1 has 100% of mass; it never fires after r0) and an upcoming choice of a1 (99.9% of mass; choice logit > 8 holds 90%, model_act==1). It is also strongly gated by time in the episode: no activity before trial 40, and it ramps up from trial 50 to 89, dropping again at 90-99. That makes it look like a clock or episode-length signal combined with a confident a1 choice after reward. The a1 choice is the agent own upcoming GO action, which is legitimate to use; no future random outcome is used. Most activity is when S1 is good (86% of mass) and value is mid-range, but that follows from choosing a1 after reward. It does not fire after unrewarded trials, on a2 choices, or early in the episode. Magnitude is not explained by the predicate; the false positives are mostly predicate-true steps at the low edge of the time window. Dev F1 0.87 (0.82 with the simpler cutoff ep_trial >= 50).

issues: The claims that it only fires at GO and only after a reward hold up. Phase GO holds 100% of the activation mass and prev_reward==1 holds 100%. It never fires at D1 or D2 or after an unrewarded trial.

Systematic false-positive class: a reward at S2 (prev_state==2) followed by choosing a1 late in the episode. The original predicate gives precision 0.0 on these 2672 dev steps; the feature never fires there. The label's 'GO step after a rewarded trial' therefore overclaims. The previous reward has to have been earned in S1.

The same split by transition: prev_common==0 & prev_action==1 (a1, rare to S2, rewarded) has precision 0.0 on 2664 steps. prev_common==0 & prev_action==2 (a2, rare to S1, rewarded) has precision 0.46. prev_common==1 & prev_action==1 has precision 0.89. So the dependence is on the rewarded state (S1), not on the transition type.
Lower precision at rel +1 (0.60) comes from the same effect. Cores are balanced over rare and common patterns, so the trial after the core more often follows a rare-rewarded trial that ended in S2.
Saying the S1-good bias (86% of mass) simply 'follows from choosing a1 after reward' is incomplete. The feature specifically needs the reward to have come from S1.

Minor point that does not affect firing: magnitude decays over long streaks of rewarded a1 trials (e.g. 0.49, 0.37, 0.27, 0.22, 0.20). It is largest on the first S1 reward after an unrewarded trial, and long streaks account for many of the remaining false positives (precision about 0.70 after 3 or more consecutive rewards).

Adding prev_state != 2 (which keeps rel -3, where prev_state is unknown) raises precision with no loss of recall. Test F1 rises from 0.858 to 0.884 (precision 0.845, recall 0.927, mass recall 0.98). Using model_act==1 instead of action==1 gives test F1 0.886. The rest of the predicate uses only observed variables and the agent's own choice.
skeptic.revised_label: GO step after a reward earned in S1, when the agent confidently chooses a1 again, late in the episode (trials ~55-94); silent after a reward in S2
